questions.stem: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point 40m away is 30°. Find the height of the tower.
questions.explanation: B is correct. tan(angle) = height/distance. height = distance × tan(angle) = 40 × tan30° = 40 × (1/√3) = 40/√3 = 40√3/3 metres ≈ 23.1m. Rationalise: 40/√3 × √3/√3 = 40√3/3.

questions.stem: From the top of a cliff 100m high, the angle of depression of a boat is 30°. How far is the boat from the base of the cliff?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Angle of depression from cliff top = angle of elevation from boat (alternate angles). tan30° = height/horizontal = 100/d. d = 100/tan30° = 100 ÷ (1/√3) = 100√3 ≈ 173.2m.

questions.stem: A pole 6m tall casts a shadow 6m long. Find the angle of elevation of the sun.
questions.explanation: B is correct. tan(angle of elevation) = opposite/adjacent = height/shadow = 6/6 = 1. tan45° = 1. Therefore angle = 45°. When height = shadow length, the angle of elevation is always 45°.

questions.stem: A man on the top of a 10m-tall building observes a car on the ground. The angle of depression is 60°. How far is the car from the building?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Angle of depression = 60°. tan60° = height/horizontal distance = 10/d. d = 10/tan60° = 10/√3 = 10√3/3 m ≈ 5.77m. NOTE: when angle of depression is HIGH (60°), the car is CLOSER to the building.

questions.stem: Two poles of heights 6m and 11m stand vertically on a plane ground. If the distance between their bases is 12m, find the distance between their tops.
questions.explanation: B is correct. The vertical difference between pole tops = 11−6 = 5m. Horizontal distance between bases = 12m. Distance between tops = √(5²+12²) = √(25+144) = √169 = 13m. This is the 5-12-13 Pythagorean triple!

questions.stem: From a point on the ground, the angles of elevation of the bottom and top of a transmission tower fixed on a building of height 20m are 45° and 60° respectively. Find the height of the tower.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Let d = horizontal distance from the point. tan45° = 20/d → d = 20m. tan60° = (20+h)/d = (20+h)/20 = √3 → 20+h = 20√3 → h = 20√3−20 = 20(√3−1) ≈ 14.64m.

questions.stem: The shadow of a tower standing on a level ground is found to be 40m longer when the sun's altitude is 30° than when it is 60°. Find the height of the tower.
questions.explanation: A is correct. At 60°: shadow = h/tan60° = h/√3. At 30°: shadow = h/tan30° = h√3. Difference = h√3 − h/√3 = h(3−1)/√3 = 2h/√3 = 40. h = 40√3/2 = 20√3 m ≈ 34.6m.

questions.stem: A boy is standing on the ground and looking at the top of a lamppost at an angle of elevation of 60°. His eye height is 1.5m and he is 3m away from the lamppost. Find the height of the lamppost.
questions.explanation: B is correct. The angle of elevation is measured from eye height (1.5m). Height from eye to lamppost top = 3 × tan60° = 3√3 m. Total lamppost height = 3√3 + 1.5 (eye height) = 3√3 + 1.5 ≈ 6.7m.

questions.stem: From the top of a tower 50m high, a ball is dropped. At the same instant, another ball is thrown horizontally from the top of another tower 50m high and 100m away. The balls meet at the same height. At what height do they meet?

options.option_text: They never meet at the same height
Both balls are always at the same height at any given instant
Cannot be determined without knowing the horizontal velocity

questions.explanation: C is correct. Both balls start at 50m and both fall under the same gravitational acceleration g. The dropped ball: h = 50 − ½gt². The thrown ball (horizontal throw): h = 50 − ½gt² (same vertical component). At any given time t, both are at the SAME HEIGHT. This is a classic projectile motion insight.

questions.stem: A ladder 10m long leans against a wall. The base of the ladder is 6m from the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Ladder = hypotenuse = 10m. Base from wall = 6m. Height up wall = √(10²−6²) = √(100−36) = √64 = 8m. 6-8-10 is the 3-4-5 triple scaled by 2.
